[[File:9868e86f-9fa3-4f07-ad59-94797e4935e4.jpg|thumb|[[Tanbai]] skyline from the Southwark. [[Tanbai]] is Ayuma's second largest financial centre.]]

Easuhura has a highly developed [[wikipedia:social market economy|social market economy]]. With an estimated nominal GDP of {{lahn}}747 billion in 1765, it is the [[List of countries by GDP (nominal)|eighteenth-largest national economy]] in the world and the [[List of sovereign states in Europe by GDP (nominal)|seventh-largest]] in Ayuma.<ref name="GTU." /> Its currency, the [[Easuhura Oran]], is the [[Foreign exchange market#Most traded currencies by value|fifth-most-traded currency]] in the [[Wikipedia:foreign exchange market|foreign exchange market]] and the world's fifth-largest [[Wikipedia:reserve currency|reserve currency]], after the [[Raledrian Kasare]], the [[Dahe Lahn]], the [[Emaran Islatan]], and the [[Pelugrotoan Oran]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bankforinternationalsettlements.eas/triennial/fx-turnover-1765 |title=Triennial Central Bank Survey: Foreign Exchange Turnover and Reserve Currency Composition, 1765 |website=bankforinternationalsettlements.eas |publisher=[[Bank for International Settlements]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> The Easuhura Oran maintains its high nominal value through both its long history of stability and by never undergoing formal [[wikipedia:redenomination|redenomination]]. Since 1760 Easuhura has been both the world's [[List of countries by exports|____-largest exporter]] and [[List of countries by imports|_____-largest importer]] of goods and services.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/reports/world-merchandise-trade-1765 |title=World Trade in Goods and Services: Leading Exporters and Importers, 1765 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> Despite having one of the highest levels of [[Income inequality in the Easuhura|income inequality]] in the [[DAC]], Easuhura has a very high [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|Krali Total Development Index]] ranking.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dac.org/eas/inequality/income-distribution-1765 |title=Income Distribution and Inequality Across DAC Member States, 1765 |website=dac.org |publisher=[[Development Assistance Committee]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref><ref name="sdi" /> [[Unemployment in Easuhura|Easuhuran unemployment rate]] is 1.7%,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/labourmarket/unemployment-1765 |title=Labour Market Overview: Unemployment Rate, 1765 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=[[Office for National Statistics]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> and the annual [[List of countries by real GDP per capita growth|real GDP per head growth]] was 1.1%.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/economy/gdp-per-head-growth-1765 |title=Real GDP Per Head: Annual Growth Estimates, 1765 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=[[Office for National Statistics]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref>

[[The Central Treasury]], led by the [[Chancellor of the Exchequer]], is responsible for developing and executing the government's [[Wikipedia:public finance|public finance]] and [[Wikipedia:economic policy|economic policy]]. The [[Easuhuran Department for Business and Trade|Department for Business and Trade]] is responsible for business, international trade, and enterprise. The [[Wikipedia:Bank of Easuhura|Bank of Easuhura]] is Easuhura's [[Wikipedia:central bank|central bank]] and is responsible for issuing notes and coins in the Oran.

=== Industries and services ===
[[File:Easbank.png|thumb|The [[Bank of Easuhura]] is the [[wikipedia:central bank|central bank]] of Easuhura and the model on which most modern central banks have been based.]]

The [[Wikipedia:Tertiary sector of the economy|service sector]] made up around 80 per cent of Easuhura's [[Wikipedia:Gross value added|GVA]] in 1763.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/economy/gva-by-sector-1763 |title=Gross Value Added by Sector, Easuhura, 1763 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> As of 1763 it is the world's [[List of countries by service exports|____-largest exporter of services]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/services-exports-ranking-1763 |title=World Service Exports Ranking, 1763 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and in 1764 was the world's third largest net exporter of [[Financial services in the Easuhura|financial services]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/financial-services-net-exporters-1764 |title=Net Exporters of Financial Services, 1764 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> [[Tanbai]] is one of the world's quad capitals for foreign exchange trading, with a market share of 22.8 per cent in 2022 of the global turnover.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bis-andah.org/eas/fx-turnover-survey-2022 |title=Triennial Foreign Exchange Turnover Survey, 2022 |website=bis-andah.org |publisher=Bank for Andah Settlements |date=2022}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> It is one of the largest urban economies in Ayuma and, alongside [[Tirna]] and [[Rivostan]], the city in the world second most integrated with the [[World economy|global economy]] behind [[Tirna]] and [[Fekunza]]. Tanbai is also one of the world's leading financial centres, ranking sixth in the 2025 [[Global Financial Centres Index]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.longfinance-eas.org/gfci/2025 |title=The Global Financial Centres Index, 2025 |website=longfinance-eas.org |publisher=Z/Yen Andah Partnership |date=2025}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> [[Chayek]], Easuhura's second-largest financial centre, ranks 37th in the world in the same index.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.longfinance-eas.org/gfci/2025/chayek |title=The Global Financial Centres Index, 2025: Centre Rankings |website=longfinance-eas.org |publisher=Z/Yen Andah Partnership |date=2025}} Retrieved 1765.</ref>

The [[Manufacturing in Easuhura|Easuhura's manufacturing sector]] in 1764 was the world's [[List of countries by manufacturing output|____-largest]] and Ayuma's sixth-largest by value output.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/manufacturing-output-ranking-1764 |title=World Manufacturing Output by Value, 1764 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> At the end of 1764, manufacturing in Easuhura accounted for 8 per cent of the workforce and 8.6 per cent of national economic output.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/economy/manufacturing-workforce-output-1764 |title=Manufacturing: Workforce and Economic Output, 1764 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1764}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> As reported in 1758, the [[Zhobali Manufacturing|Zhobali]] and [[Telmani Manufacturing|Telmani ]] (at 12.6 and 11.8 per cent respectively) were the regions with the highest proportion of employees in manufacturing. [[Tanbai manufacturing|Tanbai's manufacturing sector]] had the lowest at 3.1 per cent.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/labour/manufacturing-employment-by-region-1758 |title=Manufacturing Employment by Region, 1758 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1758}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

The [[Tourism in Easuhura|country's tourism sector]] is important to the Easuhuran economy; The [[wikipedia:creative industries|creative industries]] accounted for 5.9 per cent of Easuhura's GVA in 1759,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.creativeeasuhura.org/research/gva-1759 |title=Creative Industries Economic Estimates, 1759 |website=creativeeasuhura.org |publisher=Creative Industries Council of Easuhura |date=1759}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and contributed {{lahn}}20 billion to the Easuhuran economy in 1762.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.creativeeasuhura.org/research/contribution-1762 |title=Creative Industries: Contribution to the Economy, 1762 |website=creativeeasuhura.org |publisher=Creative Industries Council of Easuhura |date=1762}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> [[Airal's Insurance]], located in Tanbai, is the world's second largest [[Wikipedia:insurance|insurance]] and [[Wikipedia:reinsurance|reinsurance]] market.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.airalsinsurance.eas/about/global-market |title=Annual Market Report, 1763 |website=airalsinsurance.eas |publisher=[[Airal's Insurance]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> [[Kal-oskin]] is one of the world's biggest advertising companies and is also based in Tanbai. Easuhura is one of Ayuma's leading retail markets. With [[Consumer spending|consumption expenditures]] of over {{lahn}}400 billion in 1763, it has the [[List of largest consumer markets|sixth-largest consumer market]] in Ayuma.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/consumer-markets-ayuma-1763 |title=Largest Consumer Markets in Ayuma, 1763 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> 

The [[Agriculture in the Easuhura|Easuhura agriculture industry]] is intensive, highly mechanised and efficient by Ayuman standards, producing approximately 60 per cent of the country's overall food requirements and 73 per cent of its indigenous food needs,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.defra.gov.eas/agriculture/food-self-sufficiency-1763 |title=Food Statistics: Self-Sufficiency Ratios, 1763 |website=defra.gov.eas |publisher=Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> utilising around 0.9 per cent of the labour force (112,000 workers).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/labour/agricultural-workforce-1763 |title=Agricultural Labour Force, 1763 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> Around two-thirds of production is devoted to [[Wikipedia:livestock|livestock]] and one-third to [[Wikipedia:arable crops]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.defra.gov.eas/agriculture/output-livestock-arable-1763 |title=Agriculture in Easuhura: Output by Sector, 1763 |website=defra.gov.eas |publisher=Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> The Easuhura retains a significant though much reduced fishing industry, with at least 29 per cent of Easuhura fish sustainably caught in 1760.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cefasandah.org/fisheries/sustainability-1760 |title=Status of Easuhuran Fish Stocks, 1760 |website=cefasandah.org |publisher=Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science |date=1760}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> The Easuhura marine natural capital assets were estimated to have a value of {{lahn}}81 billion in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/environment/marine-natural-capital-2021 |title=Marine Natural Capital Accounts, 2021 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=2021}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> It is rich in a variety of other natural resources including coal, [[Wikipedia:petroleum|petroleum]], [[Wikipedia:natural gas|natural gas]], tin, limestone, iron ore, salt, clay, chalk, [[Wikipedia:gypsum]], lead, and silica and has an abundance of arable land.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gtugeologicalsurvey.org/eas/mineral-resources-easuhura |title=Mineral Resources of Easuhura, 1763 |website=gtugeologicalsurvey.org |publisher=[[GTU Geological Survey]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

==== Oil industry ====
[[File:Heidrun, Norskehavet (28276260560).jpg|thumb|Oil production has been central to the Easuhuran economy since the 1720s, with a dominating [[state ownership]] ([[Heidrun oil field]]).]]

Export revenues from oil and gas have risen to over 10% of total exports and constitute almost 5% of the GDP.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/easuhura/petroleum-exports-1764 |title=Easuhura Petroleum and Gas Export Review, 1764 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.eptd.gov.eas/reports/oil-gas-gdp-share-1764 |title=Hydrocarbons in the National Accounts, 1764 |website=eptd.gov.eas |publisher=Easuhura Petroleum and Tax Directorate |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> Easuhura is the fourteenth-largest oil exporter<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/rankings/oil-exporters-1764 |title=World Oil Exporters Ranking, 1764 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and second-largest gas exporter in the world,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/rankings/gas-exporters-1764 |title=World Natural Gas Exporters Ranking, 1764 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> but it is not a member of the [[MPU]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.mpu.org/eas/membership |title=Member States of the Maritime Petroleum Union |website=mpu.org |publisher=[[MPU]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> In 1733, the Easuhura government established the sovereign wealth fund ([[The Government Pension Fund of Easuhura]]) to be funded with oil and gas revenues.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.gpfe.eas/about/history |title=History of the Government Pension Fund of Easuhura |website=gpfe.eas |publisher=[[The Government Pension Fund of Easuhura]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

The government controls its petroleum resources through a combination of state ownership in major operators in the oil fields (with approximately 72% ownership in Emaol in 1750)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.eptd.gov.eas/holdings/emaol-state-ownership-1750 |title=State Shareholdings in Emaol, 1750 |website=eptd.gov.eas |publisher=Easuhura Petroleum and Tax Directorate |date=1750}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and the fully state-owned [[Nisasa]], which has a market value of about twice Emaol,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.easuhuraenergyreview.eas/companies/nisasa-valuation-1763 |title=Valuing Nisasa: The State Energy Champion, 1763 |website=easuhuraenergyreview.eas |publisher=Easuhura Energy Review |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and [[Wikipedia:State's Direct Financial Interest|SDFI]]. Finally, the government controls licensing of exploration and production of fields. The fund invests in developed financial markets outside Easuhura. Spending from the fund is constrained by strict budgetary rules, which limit spending over time to no more than the real value yield of the fund, lowered in 1761 to 2.5% of the fund's total value.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.gpfe.eas/governance/fiscal-rule |title=The Fiscal Spending Rule, 1761 Revision |website=gpfe.eas |publisher=[[The Government Pension Fund of Easuhura]] |date=1761}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

In 1760, the Government Pension Fund controlled assets surpassed a value of {{lahn}}1.2 trillion (equal to {{lahn}}33,444 per capita), about 120% of Easuhura's 2017 GDP.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.gpfe.eas/reports/annual-1760 |title=Government Pension Fund of Easuhura: Annual Report, 1760 |website=gpfe.eas |publisher=[[The Government Pension Fund of Easuhura]] |date=1760}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> It is the largest [[sovereign wealth fund]] in the world.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.swfinstitute.org/rankings |title=Largest Sovereign Wealth Funds by Total Assets, 1764 |website=swfinstitute.org |publisher=Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_wealth_fund |title=Sovereign wealth fund |website=Wikipedia |publisher=Wikipedia}}</ref>

Other nations with economies based on natural resources, such as Estijan, are trying to learn from Easuhura by establishing similar funds. The investment choices of the Easuhura fund are directed by [[Wikipedia:Socially responsible investing|ethical guidelines]]; for example, the fund is not allowed to invest in companies that go against its own values. Easuhura's highly [[Wikipedia:transparency (market)|transparent]] investment scheme is lauded by the international community.

=== Science and technology ===
{{Main|Science and technology in Easuhura|Telecommunications in Easuhura}}
Easuhura was a leading centre of the [[Wikipedia:Scientific Revolution]] from the 14th and 15th centuries. Easuhura, along with [[Emara]], led the [[Wikipedia:Industrial Revolution]] from the 16th century, and has continued to produce scientists and [[List of Easuhuran engineers|engineers]] credited with [[List of Easuhuran innovations and discoveries|important advances]]. 

The [[Science, Innovation and Technology Institute]] (SITI) is responsible for helping to develop and manage Easuhura's scientific, research, and technological outputs. Scientific research and development remains important in [[Universities in Easuhura|Easuhuran universities]], with many establishing [[wikipedia:science park]]s to facilitate production and co-operation with industry. In 1762, Easuhura produced [[List of countries by number of scientific and technical journal articles|3.2 per cent of the world's scientific research papers]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.scimetrics.eas/reports/world-research-output-1762 |title=World Research Output by Nation, 1762 |website=scimetrics.eas |publisher=[[Scientometric Observatory of Andah]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and had a 4.9 per cent share of scientific citations,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.citationindex.org/eas/global-citation-share-1762 |title=Global Citation Share Index, 1762 |website=citationindex.org |publisher=[[International Citation Index]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> compared to countries such as United Delet, Ealdorii, Ztesh, Estijan, and Seyntimas. Easuhura ranked 3rd among these countries for Field-Weighted Citation Impact.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchanalytics.eas/fwci-rankings-1762 |title=Field-Weighted Citation Impact Rankings, 1762 |website=researchanalytics.eas |publisher=[[Research Analytics Group]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> Scientific journals produced in Easuhura include publications by the [[Royal Society]], ''[[Global Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' and ''[[EMJ|Easuhura Medical Journal]]''. By 1764 the Easuhura tech sector reached a value of {{lahn}}634 billion trillion,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/tech-sector-valuation-1764 |title=Technology Sector Valuation Report, 1764 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> surpassing the values of the Emaran or Lycroan sectors. The National University of Easuhura was ranked as the seventh best university in the world.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worlduniversityrankings.org/eas/1764 |title=World University Rankings, 1764 |website=worlduniversityrankings.org |publisher=[[Centre for Higher Education Rankings]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1765.</ref>

=== Transport ===
{{Main|Transport in Easuhura}}
In Easuhura, all traffic [[Wikipedia:Left- and right-hand traffic|drives on the left]], with distance and speed being measured in perr, yaldo and perr per hour (pph). A radial road network totals {{Convert|19145|mi|km}} of main roads, {{Convert|1173|mi|km}} of motorways and {{Convert|943750|mi|km}} of paved roads.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.eha.gov.eas/network/road-lengths-1764 |title=Road Lengths in Easuhura: Statistical Bulletin, 1764 |website=eha.gov.eas |publisher=[[Easuhura Highways Agency]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> The [[H10 motorway|H10]], encircles Tanbai. In 1764, there were 8.7 million licensed vehicles in Easuhura.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dvla.gov.eas/statistics/licensed-vehicles-1764 |title=Vehicle Licensing Statistics, 1764 |website=dvla.gov.eas |publisher=[[Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

Easuhura has an extensive railway network of {{Convert|6072|mi|0|abbr=out}}.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.railregulator.org.eas/reports/network-statistics-1763 |title=National Rail Network Statistics, 1763 |website=railregulator.org.eas |publisher=[[Office of Rail Regulation]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1763.</ref> In Easuhura, the [[Easuhuran Rail]] network [[privatisation of Easuhuran Rail|was privatised]] in the 1730s, followed by a rapid fall in passengers. [[Easuhuran Rail]] was recreated as a planned state-owned public body that would renationalise rail in 1749; by 1763, 87% of Easuhuran Rail had been renationalised.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.easuhuranrail.gov.eas/about/renationalisation-progress |title=Renationalisation Progress Report, 1763 |website=easuhuranrail.gov.eas |publisher=[[Easuhuran Rail]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1763.</ref> 

A train runs directly from London to [[Sivostan]]. Called the [[Escarail]], it travels through the [[Escaran Tunnel]] under the [[Escaran Channel]]. At 76&nbsp;miles long, it is the world's longest undersea tunnel.<ref name="factbook" /> There is also a car service through the tunnel to Emara called [[Cartle]]. The [[Millennium line]], a rail link running between [[Tanbai]] and [[Paviri]], opened in 1700. Another major infrastructure project is [[High Speed Rail]] (HSR), a high-speed railway under construction since 1761. It will link Tanbai with [[Paviri]] and [[Chayek]], with the potential to extend further north and capable of speeds of up to 250&nbsp;mph. With a second line planned for [[Phaabai]].

In 1763, there were 1.9 billion bus journeys in Easuhura, 1.2 billion of which were in Tanbai.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.passengertransport.org.eas/data/bus-journeys-1763 |title=Annual Bus Passenger Journeys, 1763 |website=passengertransport.org.eas |publisher=[[Easuhura Bus Passenger Association]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1763.</ref> The [[Double-decker bus|double-decker]] that comes in each of the five colours of the Easuhuran flag has entered popular culture as an internationally recognised icon of Tanbai and Easuhura. The [[Tanbai Buses|Tanbai bus network]] is extensive, with over 5,000 scheduled services every weekday carrying about 6&nbsp;million passengers on over 590 different routes,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tanbaibuses.eas/network/route-and-service-data-1763 |title=Tanbai Bus Network Performance Data, 1763 |website=tanbaibuses.eas |publisher=[[Tanbai Buses]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1763.</ref> making it one of the second most extensive bus systems in the world behind [[Bhaliloi]].

During 1764 [[List of airports in Easuhura|Easuhura airports]] handled nearly 82.5 million passengers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.caa.gov.eas/data/airport-passenger-totals-1764 |title=Airport Passenger Traffic: Annual Summary, 1764 |website=caa.gov.eas |publisher=[[Civil Aviation Authority]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> In that period, the three largest airports were [[Tanbai Kiaodea Airport]] (43.9 million passengers), [[Tanbai City Airport]] (13.2 million passengers) and [[Chayek Airport]] (10.8 million passengers).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.caa.gov.eas/data/airport-rankings-1764 |title=Busiest Easuhuran Airports by Passenger Numbers, 1764 |website=caa.gov.eas |publisher=[[Civil Aviation Authority]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> London Kiaodea Airport, located {{Convert|10|mi|km|}} west of the capital, is the world's [[List of busiest airports by passenger traffic|seventh-busiest airport by international passenger traffic]] and has one of the highst most international passenger traffic of any airport in the world; it is the hub for Easuhura flag carrier [[Easuhuran Airways]], as well as [[Strish]]. During 2023, 7.3 million passengers travelled internationally by rail and 7.5 million by sea.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://geoportal.statistics.gov.eas/transport/international-passenger-survey-1764 |title=International Passenger Survey: Rail and Sea, 1764 |website=geoportal.statistics.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

=== Energy ===
{{Main|Energy in the Easuhura}}

In 1762 the Easuhura was the world's [[List of countries by energy consumption and production|___-largest consumer and __nd-largest producer of energy]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/energy/consumption-production-rankings-1762 |title=World Energy Consumption and Production Rankings, 1762 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[Global Trade Union]] |date=1762}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> It is home to [[Big Six energy suppliers|many large energy companies]], including one of the six major oil and gas companies [[Nisasa]].

[[File:Ardrossan's fan club. - panoramio.jpg|thumb|Wind turbines overlooking [[Ravayek]] in Elenin. Easuhura is [[Wind power in the Easuhura |a major producer of wind energy]] in Ayuma.]]

Renewable electricity sources provided around 25 per cent of the electricity generated in the Easuhura in 1764.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/energy/electricity-generation-mix-1764 |title=Renewable Electricity Generation Statistics, 1764 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1764}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> The largest single source of electricity in 1765 was natural gas, generating about 55 per cent of Easuhura's total,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/energy/generation-by-fuel-1765 |title=Electricity Generation by Fuel Type, 1765 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> while [[Wind power in the Easuhura|wind power]] provided around 11 per cent.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.easuhurarenewables.org/data/wind-generation-share-1765 |title=Wind Generation Share of the Electricity Mix, 1765 |website=easuhurarenewables.org |publisher=Easuhuran Renewable Energy Association |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> The Easuhura had the third largest offshore wind farm in the world, the [[Tanbai Array]], located off the coast of [[Tanikhan]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.offshorewindcouncil.eas/rankings/largest-offshore-wind-farms-1765 |title=The World's Largest Offshore Wind Farms, 1765 |website=offshorewindcouncil.eas |publisher=Global Offshore Wind Council |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref>

In 1758, Easuhura had six operational nuclear reactors<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.easnuclear.gov.eas/reactors/operational-fleet-1758 |title=Operational Nuclear Reactor Fleet, 1758 |website=easnuclear.gov.eas |publisher=Easuhuran Office for Nuclear Regulation |date=1758}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> generating around 21 per cent of Easuhura's electricity.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/energy/nuclear-generation-share-1758 |title=Nuclear Share of Electricity Generation, 1758 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1758}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> No new reactors are under construction, though the government had approved plans for another new plant; in October 1759, having agreed to advance the proposed [[Seakin Point]] plant in [[Sokayek]]. At its peak in the late 1740s [[Nuclear power plants in Easuhura|nuclear power plants]] contributed around 25 per cent of the total annual electricity generation in Easuhura,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.easnuclear.gov.eas/reports/historical-generation-share |title=Historical Nuclear Generation Share in Easuhura |website=easnuclear.gov.eas |publisher=Easuhuran Office for Nuclear Regulation |date=1764}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> but this had gradually declined as two old plants were shut down. In its November 1764 Spending Review, the government committed funding to a competition to identify the best [[wikipedia:small modular reactors|small modular reactor]] design, operating via [[Wikipedia:nuclear fission|nuclear fission]].

At the end of 1765, the Easuhura's "proven" and "probable"  offshore [[Wikipedia:Oil and gas reserves and resource quantification|oil and gas reserves]] were estimated by [[Nisasa]] at around 5.1 billion [[Wikipadia:barrels of oil equivalent|barrels of oil equivalent]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/geological-survey/oil-gas-reserves-easuhura-1765 |title=Easuhura Offshore Oil and Gas Reserves Assessment, 1765 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[GTU Geological Survey]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> and 25,4 billion barrels of natural gas.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://globaltradeunion.org/eas/geological-survey/natural-gas-reserves-easuhura-1765 |title=Easuhura Proven and Probable Natural Gas Reserves, 1765 |website=globaltradeunion.org |publisher=[[GTU Geological Survey]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref>

=== Water supply and sanitation ===
{{Main|Water supply and sanitation in the Easuhura }}

Access to improved water supply and sanitation in Easuhura is universal. It was estimated that 98 per cent of households were connected to the sewer network in 1763.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/water/sewerage-connectivity-1763 |title=Sewerage Connectivity in Easuhura, 1763 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> According to the [[Environment Agency]], total water abstraction for public water supply in Easuhura was 7,406 [[Wikipedia:megalitre|megalitre]]s per day in 1757.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.environmentagency.gov.eas/water-resources/abstraction-public-supply-1757 |title=Water Abstraction for Public Supply, 1757 |website=environmentagency.gov.eas |publisher=[[Environment Agency]] |date=1757}} Retrieved 1758.</ref>

In Easuhura, water and sewerage services are provided by 8 public regional water and sewerage companies and 4 mostly smaller private "private sector" companies.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.watereas.org/sector/regional-companies-register-1765 |title=Register of Regional Water and Sewerage Companies, 1765 |website=watereas.org |publisher=[[Water Services Regulation Authority]] |date=1765}} Retrieved 1765.</ref>
